notes: The San Francisco City Planning Commission's minutes of its meetings of 1980, from volume 39 of the San Francisco Public Library's deposit at the Internet Archive (39minutesofsanfran1980san). From 1980 each meeting is printed twice: a summary of the calendar with each item's resolution number and vote, then the minutes proper; for some meetings only the summary survives in the scan, for a few only the minutes, and from March some are bound as one 'Summary and Minutes'. Pages were split from the hOCR search text on the Internet Archive page index, counting the viewer page among the leaves scandata.xml does not mark addToAccessFormats=false, and every page is dated from the meeting header it sits under. Four kinds of finding: what the Commission decided about a property, dated to the meeting that decided it; what the minutes state stood on or occupied the property; dated past facts the minutes state about a building; and landmark actions. A proposal on its own is not a finding. The minutes name applicants, owners, attorneys, objectors, commissioners and staff throughout; the reader spec (in research/sources/sf-planning-commission-minutes.md, under Reader spec) barred all of them from every field, and kept companies, institutions, named buildings and architects.

coverage.remaining: Every page of volume 39 (39minutesofsanfran1980san, labelled 1980) was read: 49 meetings, 3 January to 18 December 1980 (47 regular, the evening special meeting of 26 June at the E.R. Taylor School and the joint meeting of 1 July with the Recreation and Park Commission). The scan holds no record of meetings on 7 February or 14 August, to which cases were continued, and the minutes of 11 December break off inside the Webster Street historic district hearing (HD75.1), so its outcome is not in the volume. For many meetings only the printed summary survives, not the minutes. Next: volumes 40-58 (1994-2005), which are worth sampling before a run is sized on them; 1981-1993 are in no volume.
coverage.note: 394 OCR pages of minutes text out of 440 viewer pages (442 scanned leaves; the filter kept every page with 40 or more four-letter words or a meeting header, the header test now matching 'SUMMARY' and 'SUMMARIES' as well as 'MINUTES', and dropped only the library card, a barcode leaf and the digitization notice), read in one session by a single reader with no sub-agents. The year is the condominium-conversion year again (51 of the findings are condominium subdivisions, most conversions approved 4-3 over the same three dissenting votes), the year the neighborhood commercial special use districts were drawn, the year the school district's surplus sites (Gough, Grant, Farragut, Portola, Marshall Annex, Lucinda Weeks) were rezoned for housing, and a year of new landmark recommendations (Rothschild House, Saint Paulus Lutheran Church, Chambers Mansion, the Belt Line roundhouse, the Mining Exchange, Hammersmith Building, St. Joseph's Church, Julius' Castle, Clay Street Center, the McMullen House, the Sharon Building, the Havens Mansion).
